The respondent no.2 is present in person along with counsel and accepts notice.

6. The respondent no.2 also filed a complaint before CAW Cell which culminated into registration of present FIR bearing no. 0255/2019 wherein the petitioners were implicated.
The petitioner nos. 2 to 4 are the family members/relatives of the petitioner no.1.
The petitioners and the respondent no.2 are identified by the Investigating Officer ASI Harswaroop, P.S. Burari as well as by their respective counsel.
After conclusion of the investigation, the charge-sheet was filed and the trial is stated to be pending in the court of Ms. Reetika Jain, MM, Tis Hazari Courts, Delhi.

7. The petitioner no. 1 and the respondent no. 2 have settled their disputes vide Memorandum of Understanding/Settlement dated 21.04.2022 whereby they have agreed to dissolve their marriage by way of divorce by mutual consent as per section 13B of Hindu Marriage Act, 1955.

The petitioner no.1 has also agreed to pay Rs.7,00,000/- (Rupees Seven Lacs Only) to the respondent no.2 towards full and final satisfaction of all her claims/legal entitlements (past, present and future) including permanent alimony/maintenance/istridhan etc. other miscellaneous and legal expenses as per the schedule as mentioned in the Settlement Deed.

The petitioner no.1 has already paid Rs.6,00,000/-
to the respondent no.2 which is acknowledged by the respondent no.2.

8.

The marriage between the petitioner no.1 and the respondent no.2 has already been dissolved by way of decree of divorce by mutual consent as per section 13B (2) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 by the court of Sh. Murari Prasad Singh, Judge, Family Court, Central District, Tis Hazari Court,

sentences.text: 9. The respective counsel for the petitioners and respondent no.2 stated that the disputes between the petitioners and the respondent no.2 have already been settled vide Memorandum of Understanding/Settlement dated 21.04.2022, the terms and conditions of which have already been executed.

The marriage between the petitioner no.1 and the respondent no. 2 has already been dissolved as such, the present petition be allowed and FIR bearing no. 0255/2019 registered under sections 498A/406/34 IPC at P.S. Burari be quashed along with consequential proceedings.

10. The respondent no.2 stated that she has settled with the petitioner no.1 and his family members out of her free own will and without any force, fear and coercion and her marriage with the petitioner no.1 has already been dissolved as such, she does not have any objection if the present petition is allowed and FIR bearing no. 0255/2019 registered under sections 498A/406/34 IPC at Deepak Kumar Gosai ( Husband) & Ors vs State Of Nct Of Delhi & Anr on 9 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4408494/

12. The petitioner no.1 and the respondent no. 2
got married on 08.02.2018 and due to matrimonial differences, they are living separately since 24.09.2018 without any cohabitation.

The petitioner no.1 and the respondent no.2 have already settled their pending disputes vide Memorandum of Understanding/Settlement dated 21.04.2022, the terms and conditions of which have already been executed and the respondent no.2 has already received the entire settled amount.
